core.title: Derive component names from the artifact resource plus a capability suffix
core.given: A planned component handles an artifact whose resource segment and type are known, even if the full artifact URN is not yet final.
core.when: The planner names the component or writes its component URN.
core.then: Name the component as the PascalCase form of the artifact resource plus a capability suffix chosen by the artifact type and the component's responsibility.
prefer: Normalise the resource to PascalCase first (splitting the resource on its separators and capitalising each segment), then append the suffix.

Suffix catalogs by artifact type: events (past-tense resources) take Publisher/Emitter/Broadcaster; states (adjective resources) take Tracker/Monitor/Manager; data (noun resources) take Provider/Handler/Processor/Maker; configs take Configurator/Builder/Initializer.

An artifact-derived stem that qualifies or replaces the literal resource is acceptable, for example a stem that prefixes the artifact's aspect or uses the aspect alone; the reference does not reconcile this with the literal rule, so traceability to the artifact is the binding requirement.

One artifact may fan out to several components across sides and layer roles; a responsibility suffix outside the per-type catalogs is acceptable for its matching responsibility (Display for presentation, Validator for validation, Persister for persistence), alongside a catalog suffix such as Maker at the domain role.
Let the name describe the capability to handle the artifact.
avoid: A suffix unrelated to the artifact type.
Names not traceable to the handled artifact.
core.why: Mechanical derivation from the artifact resource keeps component names predictable and traceable to the artifact they handle, while the type-driven suffix encodes the component's capability.
evidence: For each planned component, the reviewer identifies the handled artifact, takes its resource segment, and confirms the name starts with the PascalCase resource or an artifact-derived stem traceable to the artifact.

The suffix is in the catalog for the artifact's type, or is an accepted responsibility suffix for the matching responsibility (Display for presentation, Validator for validation, Persister for persistence); a suffix contradicting the artifact type fails.
The component name is PascalCase and is reused verbatim in the component URN, whose shape the profile defines.
verification: No automated implementation exists; verification is reviewer-based per the evidence items, and any automated name/suffix check would be new.
A future check needs a diff-level observer over plan artifacts that extracts new/renamed component names and the artifact resource and type they handle; no such observer exists yet.

The check identifies the artifact's resource segment per the stack's artifact-URN identifier grammar (profile: urn.grammar#artifact_resource), and confirms the name is the PascalCase resource or an artifact-traceable stem.

The check accepts per-type catalog suffixes plus the established responsibility suffixes for their matching responsibilities, and flags non-PascalCase names and suffixes that contradict the artifact type.

When the artifact type is not explicit, it may be inferred from the resource's form: past-tense resources suggest events, adjective resources states, noun resources data, and configuration-like resources configs.

The check does not cover naming the artifact itself (a separate, prerequisite convention) and does not apply to unplanned code-level names such as internal helpers, variables or test files; it applies during planning to plan artifacts, not while coding.

neutralityNotes: The convention is methodology-level (naming planned components from plan-artifact data), so almost everything is neutral. PascalCase and the capability-suffix catalogs (Publisher/Emitter/Broadcaster, Tracker/Monitor/Manager, Provider/Handler/Processor/Maker, Configurator/Builder/Initializer, plus the responsibility suffixes Display/Validator/Persister) are kept in the core: they are plain-language naming vocabulary that binds no runtime, framework, language or file syntax, and no target stack evidence suggests they need a profile idiom. The two profile-dependent parts are the component URN shape (urn.component) and the artifact-URN identifier grammar from which the resource segment is extracted (urn.grammar#artifact_resource, a map entry of urn.grammar; the Bun values are 'after the colon, final segment for dotted URNs'). The Bun text supplies no actual event/state/data/config artifact URN shape, so no per-artifact urn.<artifact> key is required. 'Sides' (frontend/backend) are generalised to 'sides and layer roles' since the vocabulary has no side concept. All concrete worked examples (stem examples, the Choice* fan-out family, PascalCase mappings, the 'choiceHandler' counter-example) are intentionally not repeated in the core; bun.json is delivered as the reference example, so the instantiated obligation is unchanged. The rule has no automated implementation (implementation.type: none); core verification records that and what a future check must tolerate.
